thread_analysis.thread_summary: Internal Allion thread (Mochizuki, Wang/Jun, Sakai, with AJ Bluetooth Group) discussing an unusually problematic Bluetooth profile test engagement for Denso Ten's automotive IVI/HMI head unit, where the DUT's unstable behavior (failed Bluetooth pairing screen transitions, lock-ups requiring power cycling, non-functional volume knob) led to over 100 Fail/Inconclusive results across 7 profiles including IOPT. The customer requested extensive per-item debug log collection to support their own analysis, which Allion's engineer performed (32 hours) without first quoting it, prompting an internal policy discussion about testing scope boundaries.
all_questions_found: (Internal) Should customer-requested per-item debug log collection beyond standard PTS-generated logs be included in the base certification testing fee, or billed as separate design verification work?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Standard Bluetooth logo certification testing scope is PTS-tool-based testing plus the PTS-generated Pass/Fail/Inconclusive logs that come with it automatically; additional custom debug logging requested by a customer for their own root-cause analysis is design verification work outside this scope. The DUT exhibited multiple instability issues (failed pairing UI transitions, full lock-ups requiring extended power-off periods, non-functional volume control) that likely contributed to the unusually high Fail/Inconclusive count, and Allion recommended the customer not treat Fail results as final until the DUT's stability issues were resolved.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Scope boundaries for certification testing services should be defined by the testing tool and method (PTS) rather than by customer request volume; once a request exceeds the PTS-log-provision baseline, it should trigger a separate quote regardless of whether it 'feels like' an extension of the same testing activity.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Without a clear scope boundary, customers experiencing high Fail/Inconclusive counts (often due to their own product instability) could repeatedly request extensive uncompensated debug support from the test lab, eroding margins and creating ambiguous service expectations.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Allion's engineer performed approximately 32 hours of customer-requested custom debug log collection without first proposing or obtaining a separate quote, which senior staff (Sakai) identified after the fact as work that should have been scoped as design verification rather than absorbed within standard testing.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a testing engagement scope expands due to customer requests for non-standard support (especially driven by product instability issues outside the lab's control), proactively quote the additional work separately at the time of request rather than performing it first and reconciling scope boundaries only after significant unbudgeted hours have already been spent.
